title: Rice-Stuffed Vine Leaves
subtitle: slow-cooked in a lemony sauce
description: Vine leaves filled with a herby tomato rice mixture, rolled and simmered slowly in a lemony sauce.

steps.text: Bring a pot of water to the boil. Blanch the vine leaves in batches of 10 for 2 minutes and remove. If using preserved leaves there is no need to blanch: remove from the jar, separate and rinse well, then soak in a bowl with a little vinegar for 10 minutes and rinse again.
Par-cook the rice: put the rice, oil, salt and water in a pot and cook for about 5 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Transfer the rice to a bowl. Add the diced tomatoes, parsley, mint, salt, black pepper and allspice and mix.
Roll the leaves: lay a vine leaf on the bench rough side down. Place a line of filling at the base, fold in both sides and roll up. Repeat with all the leaves.
Line the base of a wide pot with a few vine leaves. Pack the rolls snugly on top, side by side.
Make the sauce by mixing the sauce ingredients in a bowl, then pour it over the leaves.
Place a heatproof plate on top of the rolls to keep them in place while cooking.
Cover the pot and cook over low heat for at least 1 hour 30 minutes, checking occasionally and adding a little water if the liquid runs low.
